study.question: Does preserving a fixed uniform mass floor for every event within occupied match groups improve the utility of target-conditioned retrieval, beyond matched context-query retrieval and both frozen source bests?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: balanced_target AUC0.6202303849 exceeds balanced_context0.6200080603 and balanced_uniform0.6199768224 only slightly in the available seed. Its candidate-supplied first512 diagnostics show entropy1.84225 versus3.95928 for balanced_uniform, 118.12 visible events on average, and L1 distance1.30529 from group-uniform weights. These measurements motivate, but do not establish, harmful within-group concentration. A fixed uniform floor may retain distributed evidence while learned residual weights still select target-relevant events. This specifically changes within-group coverage; prior density/groupnorm changes changed inter-group allocation. No new-information, novelty or proven-overfitting claim.

nearest_work.source_ref: paper:din; content-sha256:5fee25f33f375e51b3ee9417d376ff9dbe2ea3628c932a7679ddfeb0feaaade2; primary section4.3 lines250-277 and Eq3, read via tools.py
nearest_work.difference: Inherit local query-key relevance and weighted history pooling. DIN abandons softmax to retain interest intensity; the local baseline already differs by using softmax, separate coarse fields, group priors and norm matching. This study tests a within-group uniform/learned convex mixture, not a DIN reproduction.

Inherit all parameters and original features; replace only final event weights w by (1-rho)w+rho*u at rho0.5, where u is uniform within groups with equal occupied-group mass. Floor0 controls are exact algebraic replacements; no extra head.

Existing uniform endpoint disables scorer gradients. New floor0.5 retains half learned weighting and active scorer gradients, so the old endpoint is useful context but not the sole active-capacity control.

study.proposed_difference: Four cells: floor_target (candidate), floor_context, free_target, free_context. For valid event i in group g of size n_g with K occupied groups, u_i=1/(K*n_g), w_i=(1-rho)*softmax_g(score_i)/K+rho*u_i. rho is fixed prospectively to0.5 or0; no sweep. Floors preserve each group mass1/K and all empty groups at0. Every valid event gets at least rho/(K*n_g). All cells execute the same operations, scorer, allocation and head. Query source is crossed to identify whether any benefit requires conditioning. This is an attention shrinkage/regularization experiment, not an asserted original architecture. No broad literature priority is claimed; registry smoothing search had no hit, which is missing evidence.
predictions: At fixed scores, floor weights preserve group mass, are halfway to u in L1, and have no lower entropy than free weights; these are implementation predictions, not empirical mechanism proof. Norm matching is nonlinear, so summary/logit contraction is not predicted.
Primary utility: floor_target improves full validation AUC over paired_match0.6191087654, target_separate0.6153351064, balanced_target0.6202303849 and matched free_target.

Conditioning support requires floor_target>floor_context and report interaction (floor_target-free_target)-(floor_context-free_context). An equal smoothing gain in both queries supports generic regularization only.

Secondary outcomes: report unweighted logloss, total/embedding/dense parameters, host wall and GPU allocation, train examples, memory, throughput and batch p50/p95. Equal training passes establish recipe matching; matched parameter shapes do not establish equal compute.

Host predeclared history-length slices (empty,1-16,17-64,>64) and category-match presence may locate effects, with provided counts; no per-slice significance or selective winner claim. Fixed first512 diagnostics only verify local behavior.
falsifiers: Floor_target fails to exceed matched free_target or balanced_target: incremental utility unsupported, even if it exceeds older sources.
Floor/context matches or beats floor/target, or query advantage vanishes on paired repeats: conditioning-specific explanation unsupported.
No entropy improvement or floor/mass/padding violations at fixed scores beyond float tolerance: implementation failure; do not score as a valid mechanism test.
Improvement is confined to logloss while AUC declines: calibration/secondary tradeoff, not primary success.
Paired seed variation or user-cluster intervals cover the apparent gain: preliminary unresolved evidence. If host cannot supply bootstrap, do not invent it.
alternative_explanations: Concentration may be useful selection; entropy has not been independently shown to be pathological. Uniform mixture could erase useful rare-event distinctions.
Mixture changes score-gradient magnitude and effective expressiveness although allocated and active parameter shapes match. A gain could be optimization/regularization rather than evidence retention.
Norm matching can amplify direction changes and alter classifier use; lower weight concentration need not reduce output sensitivity.
First512 diagnostic cohort is small and potentially unrepresentative; low target/context gain may reflect redundancy of exact match groups.
Seed/checkpoint variation, winner selection across many validation branches and static snapshot temporal uncertainty; independent confirmation is limited.

Recent negative trajectories: raw magnitude, per-group normalization, density weighting, group slots/collapse, and all four explicit product/addition cells failed to improve the balanced_target AUC. Their failures constrain these implementations, not all readout mechanisms. Latest declared UniDot-inspired explicit interaction did execute and produced nonzero feature/logit changes, but all four AUCs lost; declared use is not mechanism confirmation.
